paragraphs: Rabban Gamliel, son of our holy master, Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi. Because his father wished him to be patriarch after him, he established him in the Mishnah, Avot chapter 2, with the title Rabban. (See Asarah Maamarot, treatise Chikkur Din, part 2, chapter 19, in Yad Yehudah, section 41.) Abarbanel writes: How was this mishnah, which Gamliel stated when he was patriarch after his father Rabbi’s death, written within the compilation of the Mishnah that Rabbi made during his lifetime? One may say that he stated it during his father’s lifetime, and his father wrote it in the name of his son Gamliel; when he became patriarch after Rabbi’s death, they added the word Rabban because of the patriarchate. Or this mishnah was added after Rabbi’s death; you will find something similar in Pesachim. (See above, Rabbi Yehudah Nesia: it seems preferable that the sages of the generation added it to the Mishnah afterwards. But the aforementioned Yad Yehudah writes that to the master—meaning the author of Asarah Maamarot—it seems preferable that Rabbi himself wrote his son’s words; see there.) He was his eldest son and succeeded his father in humility; his brother Rabbi Shimon was greater than he in wisdom (see his entry): Ketubbot 103b. Shalshelet HaKabbalah says, “Rabbi commanded that his younger son Gamliel should be patriarch, because he was very humble, although his elder son Rabban Shimon was wiser.” End of quotation. He testified falsely. He was the last of the Tannaim. Wherever Rav Safra teaches in the name of “one of Rabbi’s house,” it is this Gamliel (see his entry). In Chullin 106a he ate food kept in purity, and Rabbi Yochanan questioned him there. In Shabbat 151b it is taught: Gamliel Berabbi says, “Whoever has compassion on creatures is shown compassion from heaven.” (See above, Gamliel of Yavneh, who too is called Gamliel Berabbi.) Ketubbot 10b: he seated her over the opening of a barrel. Menachot 84b: Gamliel bar Rabbi. Rabbi Yehudah Nesia was his son, and Hillel his son (see his entry). Yuchasin writes: “Rabban Gamliel: in Sefer HaGeonim, of blessed memory, he mentioned this order: our holy master; his son Gamliel; his son Yehudah Nesia, who instituted the intercalation”—there is a scribal error here, for Hillel, son of Rabbi Yehudah Nesia (see his entry), instituted the intercalation—“as Rabbi Shimon bar Tzemach Duran cites in his commentary on the Azharot; Gamliel, son of this Hillel; his son Yehudah; and the later Gamliel, in year 530 of the era of contracts.” End of quotation. See part 1, year 4118, what I wrote there concerning this, for there is a scribal error here. See Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the Elder, what is written there.
